# AuditLedger: a durable synthetic allocation ledger

Implement a Go HTTP backend for synthetic tenant-scoped resource units. There is no frontend, external service, real money, authentication provider, or clock-based expiration. The hard part is making posting, reservations, retries, historical reads, migration, and concurrent writers obey one coherent model.

Use Go 1.26.3 and the pinned `modernc.org/sqlite v1.59.0` dependency. The starter contains only process/driver scaffolding and an old-format fixture producer, not a solution. Build with `go build -o server ./cmd/server`. Run with `./server --db PATH --listen HOST:PORT`. The database must persist all state and retries across restarts. Two processes must be able to serve the same database concurrently. Use ordinary local SQLite locking; no process-global state may be the source of truth. Implement graceful process termination. Stay within this repository; do not modify the task or evaluation tools.

## Wire contract

All bodies and responses are JSON. Request bodies are objects; invalid JSON, wrong types, unknown request fields, trailing JSON, missing required fields, and out-of-range values return 400 `invalid`. A missing body is invalid on writes. Integer amounts must be 1..1,000,000,000; opening balances are 0..1,000,000,000. Account balances and reservations must remain in the range 0..9,000,000,000,000,000 (check addition before overflow). Names and tenant IDs match `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,40}`. Tenant identity comes from mandatory `X-Tenant` on every endpoint except health. Missing or invalid tenant returns 400 `invalid`. All IDs are opaque nonempty strings and unique within a tenant. Timestamps are unnecessary. Unknown response fields are permitted.

Each mutating request requires `Idempotency-Key` matching `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,80}`. Its scope is the tenant across ALL write endpoints. Store a successful operation's HTTP status and JSON result atomically with its effects. The same key, path, and semantically identical body (JSON field order/whitespace irrelevant) replays the original status/result, including original account versions, despite later changes. Any changed path/body using a successful key returns 409 `idempotency_conflict`. Failed operations do not consume the key. Replays precede current-state version/business checks. Concurrent identical requests produce one effect and the same result. Do not cache failures.

Errors have `{"error":{"code":"..."}}` and may include a message. Codes: 400 `invalid`; 404 `not_found` (including objects that only exist in another tenant); 409 `exists`, `version_conflict`, `insufficient`, `idempotency_conflict`, or `terminal`. Invalid supplied versions (zero/negative/noninteger/null) are 400. An omitted version imposes no optimistic condition; a supplied version must equal the current version or return 409 `version_conflict`. All specified conditions within a batch observe staged changes in request order. Missing accounts are 404 before balance checks. No partial effects or cached successes on any failure.

An account object is `{"name":"A","balance":100,"reserved":20,"available":80,"version":3}`. Balance includes reserved units; available = balance - reserved. A new account starts at version 1. Every affected account advances exactly once per operation touching it (one transfer, hold creation/capture/release, or reversal); batch transfers advance separately in sequence. Reads never advance versions. All modifications and emitted entries are atomic.

## Endpoints (11 routes)

1. `GET /health` -> 200 `{"ok":true}` only after the database is usable/migration completed.
2. `POST /accounts` body `{"name":"A","opening":100}` -> 201 `{"account":ACCOUNT}`. Duplicate name -> 409 `exists`. Emit one opening entry even for zero opening.
3. `GET /accounts/{name}` -> 200 `{"account":ACCOUNT}` or 404.
4. `POST /transfers` body `{"from":"A","to":"B","amount":7,"from_version":1,"to_version":1}` -> 201 `{"transfer":{"id":ID,"from":"A","to":"B","amount":7,"reversed":false},"accounts":[FROM_ACCOUNT,TO_ACCOUNT]}`. Versions optional. Accounts must differ. Debit available units only; post balance changes -amount/+amount and increment both versions.
5. `POST /batches` body `{"transfers":[TRANSFER_REQUEST,...]}` -> 201 `{"transfers":[TRANSFER_OBJECT,...],"accounts":[ACCOUNT,...]}`. 1..20 transfers, sequentially applied atomically. Accounts list contains each touched account once sorted by name, with its final state. A later error rolls back earlier transfers, entries, and versions. Replays preserve all generated IDs.
6. `POST /holds` body `{"account":"A","amount":9,"version":2}` -> 201 `{"hold":{"id":ID,"account":"A","amount":9,"state":"active"},"account":ACCOUNT}`. Version optional. Reserve available units; balance unchanged, reserved increases, version advances.
7. `POST /holds/{id}/capture` body `{"to":"B","from_version":3,"to_version":2}` -> 200 `{"hold":HOLD,"transfer":TRANSFER,"accounts":[FROM_ACCOUNT,TO_ACCOUNT]}`. Versions optional. Capture the entire active hold: reduce source reserved and balance by hold amount, credit destination balance, advance both versions. Destination must differ. Emit transfer and entries in the same transaction. Hold state becomes `captured`. Capture/release of terminal hold with a different key -> 409 `terminal`.
8. `POST /holds/{id}/release` body `{"version":3}` (or `{}`) -> 200 `{"hold":HOLD,"account":ACCOUNT}`. Release all reserved units, leave balance unchanged, advance source version, state `released`.
9. `POST /transfers/{id}/reverse` body `{"from_version":4,"to_version":3}` (or `{}`) -> 200 `{"transfer":ORIGINAL_TRANSFER,"reversal":TRANSFER,"accounts":[ORIGINAL_FROM_ACCOUNT,ORIGINAL_TO_ACCOUNT]}`. Only an unreversed ordinary or capture/batch transfer can reverse. Debit the original destination's available amount and credit the original source. Both versions advance. Original now has `reversed:true`; reversal has exchanged from/to, same amount, `reversed:false`. A reversal itself cannot reverse (409 `terminal`). The original and reversal use distinct transfer IDs; one idempotency key still belongs to the tenant-wide write-key namespace. A second reversal of the original -> 409 `terminal`. Holds stay captured. Preserve original entries; emit compensating entries.
10. `GET /entries?after=0&limit=50&snapshot=N` -> 200 `{"entries":[ENTRY,...],"snapshot":N,"next_after":K,"has_more":BOOL}`. Each ENTRY has `seq` positive tenant-local integer, `account`, `kind` (`opening`, `transfer`, `hold`, `capture`, `release`, `reversal`), signed integer `balance_delta`, signed integer `reserved_delta`, and `operation_id` nonempty (the transfer ID for transfer/capture/reversal, hold ID for hold/release; opening IDs may be independently generated). Transfer/capture/reversal emit source then destination entries. Opening/hold/release emit one. `seq` increases with committed entries; gaps are allowed. Results ordered ascending seq. Missing after defaults 0; limit defaults 50, range 1..100; snapshot defaults current max seq (0 for empty tenant). Only entries after `after` and at/below snapshot are included; next_after is last returned seq or the supplied after. has_more considers remaining entries within snapshot. Explicit snapshot must be 0..current max seq; after must be 0..snapshot. Invalid query values/unknown query keys -> 400. Pagination fixes the history across intervening writes and restarts.
11. `GET /summary?snapshot=N` -> 200 `{"snapshot":N,"accounts":[{"name":"A","balance":100,"reserved":20,"available":80},...],"totals":{"balance":100,"reserved":20,"available":80},"entry_count":4}`. At a supplied snapshot, derive all values ONLY from entries at/below that snapshot, include accounts whose opening entry is visible, sorted by name. Default current max seq; validate snapshot as above and reject unknown query keys. This gives a stable historical summary even if present-day holds and balances differ. Every current account must agree with its current entry-derived totals. Transfers and reversals conserve total balance; holds/releases conserve balance; capture conserves balance and lowers total reserved.

Any unspecified HTTP method or route returns 404 `not_found` (405 is also allowed for a known path/wrong method). IDs/names containing separators must not resolve another tenant/path. JSON response arrays are always arrays, including empty ones.

## Genuine legacy migration

Before starting some runs, `python3 legacy/produce.py DATABASE` creates a real SQLite v1 database with `PRAGMA user_version=1`, tables:

```
legacy_accounts(tenant TEXT, name TEXT, balance INTEGER, PRIMARY KEY(tenant,name))
legacy_movements(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant TEXT, source TEXT, target TEXT, units INTEGER)
legacy_notes(key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT)
```

The producer and fixture JSON define all rows. Balances are FINAL balances after legacy movements; do not treat them as opening balances and apply movements twice. Infer each opening balance = final balance + outgoing units - incoming units, create opening entries in `(tenant,name)` order (each tenant has its own sequence, so its openings are ordered by account name), then import movements in ID order as reversible transfer objects and ordinary `transfer` entries. Imported transfer objects additionally expose integer `legacy_id` in entries' corresponding operation detail: to make them discoverable, imported transfer ENTRYs include `legacy_id`. They obey normal reversals. All migrated accounts start with version `1 + number of imported movements touching the account`. Reservations are zero. All legacy rows/tables/notes must remain intact, and user_version advances to 2. Migration is all-or-nothing, safe under two starting processes, and never repeats on restart. An empty new database also becomes version 2. No fixture-specific names/values in implementation. A separate generated fixture can use the same schema. Preserve values byte-for-byte in legacy text/blob fields; don't drop/rewrite old tables. Use no destructive database reset on errors.

## Delivery and evaluation

Deliver runnable source and a concise README explaining schema, transaction boundaries, migration, and how to run. No reference implementation is provided. The independent post-episode acceptance tool records independent grouped results and exact synthetic HTTP traces. Correctness comes before throughput; performance results from an incorrect server are diagnostic only. The meter seeds 5,000 transfers through the public batch API, giving 10,002 entries; each cell clones that populated seed. Benchmark reads (fixed historical summary) and writes use concurrency 1/16, 1-second warmup and 5-second measured windows, three repetitions, and fresh state per cell. The meter counts every started request and checks conservation, with failures retained. All data is synthetic. Do not run the performance meter concurrently with a build or model call.
